title: Raksha Mantri to undertake annual performance review of 16 DPSUs in New Delhi
body_text:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will undertake the annual performance review of 16 Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) in New Delhi on September 1, 2026, underscoring the importance of developing new indigenous technologies and enhancing exports. During the event, the CMDs of seven DPSUs - Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), BEML, and MIDHANI - will present dividend cheques for the Government's equity shares to the Raksha Mantri for the Financial Year (FY) 2025–26.
On the occasion, Shri Rajnath Singh will release four books namely ‘Aatmanirbhar DPSU - A journey of DPSUs towards Self-Reliance’; DISHA, an initiative of DPSUs for students’ hands-on awareness on defence technologies & modern manufacturing processes; Modernisation roadmap of HAL; and Indigenisation Roadmap of HAL.
Notably, the performance of DPSUs in FY 2025-26 has been commendable. Their total turnover stood at Rs 1.29 lakh crore, up 15.4% from the figure in FY 2024-25. The DPSUs recorded cumulative Profit After Tax in 2025-26 of Rs 23,136 crore, registering a growth of 15.6 % over the previous year. Remarkably, in 2025-26, DPSU’s achieved an increase of 151.2% in exports over the previous Financial Year.
****
VK/Sa vvy

enrichment.summary: Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh will conduct the annual performance review of India's 16 Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) in New Delhi on 1 September 2026. Seven DPSUs - HAL, MDL, BEL, BDL, GRSE, BEML and MIDHANI - will present FY2025-26 dividend cheques, and four books on DPSU self-reliance, student outreach (DISHA) and HAL's modernisation/indigenisation roadmaps will be released. DPSUs reported a combined turnover of Rs 1.29 lakh crore (up 15.4%), Profit After Tax of Rs 23,136 crore (up 15.6%), and a 151.2% surge in exports over the previous year.
enrichment.context:
DPSUs are central to India's Aatmanirbhar Bharat push in defence manufacturing, which aims to reduce import dependence, boost indigenous R&D, and expand defence exports (the government has set ambitious export targets running into tens of thousands of crores). Entities like HAL, BEL, MDL, BDL and GRSE are also listed companies where the government periodically reviews financial performance and disburses/receives dividends as majority shareholder. Annual performance reviews of this kind are used to track progress on indigenisation timelines, order books, and corporate governance reforms within DPSUs, which have historically faced criticism for delays and quality issues in defence production.

The reported growth figures - turnover, profit, and especially the sharp rise in exports - feed into broader policy narratives about defence sector reform, corporatisation of ordnance factories, and India's positioning as an emerging defence exporter, relevant to discussions on self-reliance in strategic sectors and public sector enterprise reform.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) whose CMDs presented dividend cheques for FY 2025-26 as mentioned in the review event?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release names HAL, MDL, BEL, BDL, GRSE, BEML and MIDHANI as the seven DPSUs presenting dividend cheques; Hindustan Shipyard Limited is not among them.

prelims_questions.question: As per the DPSU performance data for FY 2025-26 highlighted by the Ministry of Defence, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Total turnover of DPSUs declined compared to FY 2024-25
Cumulative Profit After Tax grew by about 15.6% over the previous year
Defence exports by DPSUs decreased over the previous year
Total turnover of DPSUs stood at Rs 1.29 lakh crore with 15.4% growth
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states DPSU turnover for FY 2025-26 was Rs 1.29 lakh crore, a 15.4% increase over FY 2024-25, while PAT grew 15.6% and exports grew 151.2%.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the role of Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) in achieving India's goal of self-reliance (Aatmanirbhar Bharat) in defence manufacturing. What structural and governance challenges continue to affect their performance?
Examine the significance of rising defence exports for India's strategic and economic interests. What policy measures can further strengthen the indigenous defence industrial base?

study_notes.reason: The release is largely a factual announcement of DPSU financial performance and identities, with limited analytical depth beyond generic self-reliance framing; the value lies in knowing which entities are DPSUs and their financial metrics.

prelims.point: There are 16 Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) under the Ministry of Defence, of which HAL, MDL, BEL, BDL, GRSE, BEML and MIDHANI are named as major listed ones presenting dividends.
prelims.why_important: UPSC could test identification/matching of DPSUs with their full forms and products, a recurring prelims pattern for PSU-based questions.

prelims.point: DPSUs are majority government-owned companies that pay annual dividends to the government as shareholder, reviewed via an annual performance review by the Raksha Mantri.
prelims.why_important: Tests understanding of the government's role as majority shareholder in strategic PSUs distinct from ordnance factories (which were corporatised separately).

prelims.point: FY 2025-26 DPSU financials: turnover Rs 1.29 lakh crore (up 15.4%), Profit After Tax Rs 23,136 crore (up 15.6%), exports up 151.2% over previous year.
prelims.why_important: Specific growth figures could appear in a factual/statement-based question on defence production and export performance.

mains.point: Rising DPSU turnover, profitability and exports reflect progress under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat framework in defence manufacturing, indicating reduced import dependence and improved indigenous capacity.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on evaluating progress of Aatmanirbhar Bharat in the defence sector or assessing indigenisation efforts of DPSUs.

mains.point: The sharp surge in defence exports (151.2%) supports India's positioning as an emerging defence exporter, relevant to strategic and economic diplomacy discussions.
mains.analytical_use: Can be used to discuss India's defence export strategy, target achievement, and implications for foreign policy/strategic partnerships.

mains.point: Annual performance reviews of DPSUs serve as an accountability and governance mechanism, historically relevant given past criticism of DPSUs for production delays and quality issues.
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on governance reforms in strategic PSUs, corporatisation trends, and challenges in defence production efficiency.

low_priority.point: Release of four books on DPSU self-reliance, student outreach and HAL roadmaps
low_priority.reason: Ceremonial/promotional detail with no independent testable or analytical content.
